sentence: This project studies how immune cells called macrophages help a deadly brain tumor avoid the immune system, and tries to build an immunotherapy against it.
This project builds an MRI contrast agent from iron cages and tests changes to the cages in mice to improve water solubility.
This project builds drugs that block the breakdown of hydroxyproline, which leads to kidney stones and kidney damage in people with primary hyperoxaluria.
This project tries to find out how the tumor environment can point to better cancer immunotherapy, using patient samples and mouse models.
This project studies how INTS12 controls genes in developing red blood cells and what goes wrong in a rare red cell disease.
This project studies changes in chromatin and gene activity in brain glial cells linked to opioid seeking, using CRISPR tools.
This project studies how proteins called epsins in blood vessel cells control signaling, and builds a nanoparticle therapy to help vessels regrow after stroke.
This project tries to find out which gut microbes predict when drug-resistant organisms settle in, and clear from, the gut after organ transplantation.
This project studies what a class of metalloenzymes does in bacteria that live where oxygen is scarce in the human body.
This project tests whether imaging of the eye, brain MRI and microscopic tumor imaging can show earlier signs that glioblastoma is progressing.
This project builds methods that use existing data to find effects of common drugs on cancer and Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how DNA methylation and inflammation before birth reprogram microglia, the immune cells of the brain, during development.
This project builds living biosensors from bacteria that detect DNA in dirty samples and show the result on a lateral flow strip.
This project develops imaging technologies that use light and computers, without labels, to study cancer and neurodegenerative diseases.
This project studies how Epstein-Barr virus stays in the body and returns, and how rare gene variants lead to poor control of the infection.
This project builds machine learning methods that recognize how a speaker forms an American English r sound from audio, to give speech therapy feedback.
This project builds a knowledge hypergraph and a neural network method to find which drug combinations work best for specific groups of patients.
This project studies which brain processes underlie mentalizing, a social thinking skill, in young adults with a first episode of psychosis.
This project trains deep-learning models on ultrasound images to detect polycystic ovary syndrome more accurately and sooner.
This project studies how a chromatin regulator called HMGA1 helps a hard-to-treat blood cancer grow and resist therapy, in order to develop better treatments.
